## Summary of Findings

**1. Business Segments**
3M's segment structure changed over the filing history:
- **2018 10-K**: Five segments — Industrial, Safety and Graphics, Health Care, Electronics and Energy, and Consumer [E1][E5].
- **2022 10-K / 2023 10-Q**: Four segments — Safety and Industrial, Transportation and Electronics, Health Care, and Consumer, following a 2018 realignment and subsequent consolidation [E2][E3][E4][E8].
- In July 2022, 3M announced its intention to spin off the Health Care business as a separate public company [E2][E3][E4].
- Segments are managed with substantial intersegment cost allocation and inventory transfers; management does not represent that segments would report the same operating income if run independently [E2][E5].

**2. Research & Development Spending**
- Total "research, development and related expenses": $1.821B (2018), $1.870B (2017), $1.764B (2016) [E9][E11].
- Narrower "research and development expenses" (basic scientific research and application): $1.253B (2018), $1.352B (2017), $1.248B (2016) [E9][E11].
- By 2022, R&D expenses (narrower definition) had declined to approximately $1.1 billion, versus $1.2 billion (2021) and $1.1 billion (2020) [E14].
- Capital spending guidance: 2019 expected $1.7–$1.9B [E13]; 2023 expected $1.5–$1.8B [E10], reflecting continued investment in growth, productivity, and sustainability.

**3. Environmental Liabilities**
- 3M records remediation liabilities on an undiscounted basis when probable and reasonably estimable; company expects payments to occur over periods "ranging up to 20 years" [E17][E18][E23].
- **Year-end 2018**: $25 million recorded for "environmental remediation" liabilities, plus $8 million in related insurance receivables [E24]; separately, $59 million recorded for "other environmental liabilities" tied to sites in Alabama, Minnesota, and settlement/consent orders (MPCA, ADEM) [E23].
- **Mid-2023 (10-Q)**: $32 million recorded for non-PFAS-related environmental remediation liabilities [E18]; insurance recoveries receivable of $8 million as of June 30, 2023 [E20].
- **2022 10-K**: insurance recoveries receivable also $8 million as of Dec 31, 2022 [E22]. In 2022, 3M spent approximately $317 million on environmental capital projects, with expected capital expenditures of ~$646 million in aggregate for 2023–2024 [E19]. In 2018, comparable capital environmental spending was ~$27 million, with ~$75 million expected over the following two years [E21].
- Separately, 3M disclosed a $897 million pre-tax charge ($710 million after-tax) in Q1 2018 related to resolution of an environmental matter (this appears distinct from the ongoing remediation reserve lines) [E12].
- Filings note PFAS-related and combat arms earplugs litigation are classified as "corporate special items" and are managed separately from the routine remediation liability disclosures above [E8].
- The filings state that for sites where remediation is largely complete, exposure to loss above accrued amounts is not expected to be material; for ongoing sites, the company states it cannot estimate a possible loss in excess of accruals [E20][E22].

## Summary of Findings

**1. Business Segments**
3M's segment structure changed over the filing history:
- **2018 10-K**: Five segments — Industrial, Safety and Graphics, Health Care, Electronics and Energy, and Consumer [E1][E5].
- **2022 10-K / 2023 10-Q**: Four segments — Safety and Industrial, Transportation and Electronics, Health Care, and Consumer, following a 2018 realignment and subsequent consolidation [E2][E3][E4][E8].
- In July 2022, 3M announced its intention to spin off the Health Care business as a separate public company [E2][E3][E4].
- Segments are managed with substantial intersegment cost allocation and inventory transfers; management does not represent that segments would report the same operating income if run independently [E2][E5].

**2. Research & Development Spending**
- Total "research, development and related expenses": $1.821B (2018), $1.870B (2017), $1.764B (2016) [E9][E11].
- Narrower "research and development expenses" (basic scientific research and application): $1.253B (2018), $1.352B (2017), $1.248B (2016) [E9][E11].
- By 2022, R&D expenses (narrower definition) had declined to approximately $1.1 billion, versus $1.2 billion (2021) and $1.1 billion (2020) [E14].
- Capital spending guidance: 2019 expected $1.7–$1.9B [E13]; 2023 expected $1.5–$1.8B [E10], reflecting continued investment in growth, productivity, and sustainability.

**3. Environmental Liabilities**
- 3M records remediation liabilities on an undiscounted basis when probable and reasonably estimable; company expects payments to occur over periods "ranging up to 20 years" [E17][E18][E23].
- **Year-end 2018**: $25 million recorded for "environmental remediation" liabilities, plus $8 million in related insurance receivables [E24]; separately, $59 million recorded for "other environmental liabilities" tied to sites in Alabama, Minnesota, and settlement/consent orders (MPCA, ADEM) [E23].
- **Mid-2023 (10-Q)**: $32 million recorded for non-PFAS-related environmental remediation liabilities [E18]; insurance recoveries receivable of $8 million as of June 30, 2023 [E20].
- **2022 10-K**: insurance recoveries receivable also $8 million as of Dec 31, 2022 [E22]. In 2022, 3M spent approximately $317 million on environmental capital projects, with expected capital expenditures of ~$646 million in aggregate for 2023–2024 [E19]. In 2018, comparable capital environmental spending was ~$27 million, with ~$75 million expected over the following two years [E21].
- Separately, 3M disclosed a $897 million pre-tax charge ($710 million after-tax) in Q1 2018 related to resolution of an environmental matter (this appears distinct from the ongoing remediation reserve lines) [E12].
- Filings note PFAS-related and combat arms earplugs litigation are classified as "corporate special items" and are managed separately from the routine remediation liability disclosures above [E8].
- The filings state that for sites where remediation is largely complete, exposure to loss above accrued amounts is not expected to be material; for ongoing sites, the company states it cannot estimate a possible loss in excess of accruals [E20][E22].
